NEW · ENVIRONMENT-FIRST PATTERN TEST · 26 SEP 2026

Stronger home team → main shooters

665 eligible MLS fixtures. Stronger means better season-to-date and last-five points per game. The shooting filter combines home shot creation with away shots conceded. Main shooters are the top two eligible starters by earlier shots per start.

FilterAll player-matchesLater matches (from 26 Oct 2025)
Top 2 home shooters (baseline)897/1330 (67.4%)253/362 (69.9%)
Top 2 + stronger home team326/462 (70.6%)95/130 (73.1%)
Top 2 + full home environment229/320 (71.6%)65/86 (75.6%)
Full environment + recent minutes >=70218/300 (72.7%)63/82 (76.8%)
Full environment + minutes >=70 + 4/5 recent hits150/185 (81.1%)46/57 (80.7%)
Top 2 + minutes >=70 + 4/5 hits WITHOUT environment filter523/660 (79.2%)152/184 (82.6%)

The full environment correctly identified the home side taking more shots in 118/160 matches (73.8%); later: 32/43 (74.4%).

Promising, not proven: the strict pattern hit 150/185 (81.1%), but consistent shooters without the environment filter did slightly better in later matches. The environment's extra value is not established. Retrospective, MLS-only evidence; no odds or profitability tested.

Next: freeze these two versions and compare them on fresh matches. Use confirmed starters; do not tune thresholds to this result. Existing ticket reconciliation stays unchanged.

Early repeated differences

  • The supported within-player totals separate sharply by construction: saved hits average 4.00 shots; the nine same-player misses with supported counters average 0.89.

    Descriptive only. This confirms the comparison cohort but does not identify a pre-match cause.

  • Long minutes did not guarantee 2+ shots: at least five same-player misses have supported 90-minute appearances (Joao Pedro, Ante Budimir, Rafael Navarro, Guilherme Augusto and Lionel Messi).

    Hypothesis: opportunity quality, team volume and player share may matter more than minutes after a basic playing-time threshold. Hit-side context is still missing, so this is not yet tested.

  • Supported team context now covers 15 hits and 8 same-player misses. Hit teams averaged 13.2 shots and selected players averaged a 29.2% share; misses averaged 11.5 team shots and a 9.0% player share.

    Descriptive only: post-match share contains the outcome numerator, so separation is partly induced by selecting hits and misses. Test lagged pre-match share on verified dated records before claiming predictive value. Denominator is full-match team shots, not on-field shots.

  • A goal or creative return did not ensure repeated shooting: Ante Budimir scored with his only shot; Joao Pedro had a goal and assist from one shot; Lionel Messi had two assists from one shot.

    Hypothesis: avoid using goals or general attacking involvement as a substitute for shot-volume evidence.

32 of 119 hits landed exactly on two shots. The other 87 cleared the threshold by at least one.

What we can say so far

  • Replacement labels can mislead. The original player and the displayed replacement need separate records.
  • Minutes cannot explain every miss. Eleven displayed players had 80+ provider minutes and fewer than two personal shots.
  • A report miss is not a proven lost bet. Fourteen misses have only cashed-out assessed occurrences; Gauld’s MISS is linked to a ticket marked Won.

Match dates are candidate links. Some external totals come from indexed extracts. Causes and final settlements remain unverified where evidence is missing.
